candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — health promotion, risk reduction and client education
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — tobacco cessation before surgery
candidate.educational_objective: Teach that preoperative smoking cessation reduces perioperative risk and should be encouraged before elective surgery and during recovery.

options.A: Quitting before surgery can reduce breathing and wound-healing complications, so stopping now and remaining smoke-free through recovery is beneficial
options.B: Smoking affects long-term health but has no meaningful relationship to postoperative respiratory or wound complications
options.C: It is better to continue smoking until after surgery because stopping beforehand increases surgical complications
options.D: Only clients with diagnosed chronic lung disease benefit from stopping smoking before surgery

candidate.rationale: Smoking increases perioperative pulmonary and wound-healing risk. The American College of Surgeons advises clients to quit before surgery and remain smoke-free during recovery; earlier cessation provides time for physiologic benefit.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Preoperative smoking cessation improves surgical recovery and reduces wound and respiratory risk.
candidate.source_locator: Quit Smoking before Surgery — smoking increases problems during/after surgery; quitting 4–6 weeks before surgery and staying smoke-free after surgery reduces wound complications
candidate.stem: A client who smokes daily is scheduled for elective surgery in 6 weeks and asks whether quitting now would matter. Which response by the nurse is best?
